briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been formally signed and implemented by Iran and the United States, signifying an end to military conflict between the two nations and leading to the immediate lifting of the US maritime blockade on Iran, with oil traffic resuming through the Strait of Hormuz. However, the delicate peace is immediately threatened by continued Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon and Prime Minister Netanyahu's explicit refusal to withdraw from a newly established "security zone," prompting Iran to delay its delegation's travel to Switzerland for follow-up talks.

IRAN
The Iran-US Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been signed by President Masoud Pezeshkian and US President Donald Trump, with Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also signing. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei approved the MoU, despite his initial "different view," stating his consent was based on President Pezeshkian's commitment to safeguard national rights and the Resistance Front, and to resist "excessive demands" from the US. Khamenei emphasized that future in-person talks would not imply acceptance of the enemy's position.

President Pezeshkian welcomed the Leader's message, viewing it as a framework for negotiations and a guarantee of Iran's victory, hailing the MoU as a "historic document" demonstrating a "powerful Iran." Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi appreciated the Leader's guidance and, in a call with French FM Jean-Noël Barrot, stressed US responsibility to end conflicts on all fronts, including Lebanon. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf claimed Iran gained "several times more" through negotiation than military action, warned of Iran's "hand on the trigger" against "greedy" adversaries, and stated the Strait of Hormuz would "never return to its previous conditions" but would adhere to international law. Ghalibaf also linked revenge for the "martyred leader" to the liberation of Jerusalem.

Regarding nuclear matters, the MoU stipulates Iran will not acquire nuclear weapons. US VP JD Vance asserted Iran committed to destroying its highly enriched material, stating, "Obama's deal allowed enrichment, ours won't." Iran's Foreign Ministry indicated "reducing enriched materials is now an option," but "transferring enriched nuclear materials out of the country is an unacceptable option." The issue of enrichment will be discussed in the final agreement.

The US CENTCOM has lifted the maritime blockade on Iran. Iran's Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) announced a 60-day fee-free transit period for commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, managed by the Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA.ir), requiring coordinated transit for safety. MarineTraffic.com showed an increase to nearly 20 ships passing through the Strait in the last 24 hours, up from fewer than 10 previously, including three Iranian oil tankers carrying 5 million barrels, with another 2 million barrel tanker approaching.

The Iranian delegation's planned trip to Switzerland for initial talks on implementing the MoU has been delayed, with Al-Mayadeen (close to Hezbollah) reporting this is due to "continued Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon." Pakistan's PM Sharif's visit was also canceled, with his deputy foreign minister now expected to attend.

Internally, singer Parastoo Ahmadi and eight others received sentences including 74 lashes and a 2-year ban from art and travel for performing without a hijab. The Head of Iran's largest petrochemical group reported 89% of previously shut-down petrochemical units are back in production.

ISRAEL
An IDF reservist, Master Sgt. (res.) Alexander Filin, 29, from Haifa, a combat soldier with the 36th Division's headquarters, was killed by a Hezbollah explosive device in southern Lebanon. Seven other IDF personnel were wounded in the same incident, including the deputy commander of the 36th Division (Colonel) and a battalion commander (Lieutenant Colonel), both moderately injured, along with five others lightly injured. Following the incident, the IDF conducted artillery shelling on Hezbollah infrastructure in the area.

The IDF has published an updated map of a "security zone" in southern Lebanon, extending up to 10 km deep into Lebanese territory from the border, where its forces are operating. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu affirmed that Israel would "restore security to the north" and maintain this "security zone" as long as Israel's security needs require it. Netanyahu also stressed the importance of "maintaining the important relationship with our American friends."

Netanyahu reportedly believes the final agreement with Iran will not materialize and is seeking to influence its outcome through right-wing media and members of Congress. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announced a severing of all contact with EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas, citing her alleged comparison of Israel to an "apartheid regime."

US Vice President JD Vance publicly criticized Netanyahu's cabinet for attacking President Trump, reminding them that two-thirds of Israel's defensive weapons are "built by American hands and paid for by American tax dollars." Vance urged Israel to "respect this peace process" and cautioned against "going wild" in Lebanon, calling such actions "unacceptable." A senior Israeli official close to Netanyahu stated Israel is engaged in "stubborn negotiations" with the US over its military presence in southern Lebanon and has no intention of backing down. Maariv reports indicate Israeli officials fear intensifying US pressure, potentially escalating from weapon shipment delays to an arms embargo.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Palestinian sources reported casualties, including killed and wounded, from an Israeli strike in Gaza City. In the West Bank, Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned "criminal actions of Zionist settlers, backed by the Israeli military," citing attacks on two mosques in Ramallah, assaults on homes, beatings of Palestinians, and destruction of property and farmland. An attempted smuggling of cigarettes into Gaza concealed in Pringles packages was intercepted.

LEBANON
Hezbollah fired several rockets at Israeli troops in southern Lebanon; some were intercepted, others struck near forces, with no reported injuries. Hezbollah's "Resistance Operations Room" claimed successful engagements against IDF forces attempting to advance towards Kfar Tebnit/Ali Al-Taher on 17-18 June, alleging "heavy losses" and forced IDF retreats, including targeting a Merkava tank on 18 June at 01:50 UTC. Lebanese media reported one dead and another critically wounded in an Israeli drone strike near Kfar Tebnit. The IDF confirmed artillery shelling on Hezbollah infrastructure following the killing of Master Sgt. (res.) Alexander Filin by an explosive device. Israeli airstrikes were also reported in Kfar Jouz, Harouf, Al-Sharqiyah, Zawtar, and Zebdine.

The IDF has established a "security zone" up to 10 km deep into southern Lebanon, stating it will operate there "in accordance with operational needs." Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri affirmed Lebanon's and Hezbollah's commitment to the ceasefire, conditional on Israel's "full and comprehensive" adherence. This commitment was framed in the context of the Iran-US MoU.

SYRIA & IRAQ
An unknown rocket attack targeted "Joulani gangs" positions in Al-Hawl town, Hasakah province, Syria. The Director General of Israel's Defense Ministry, Amir Baram, warned that Houthi forces in Yemen and Iraqi militias "have the ability to infiltrate Israel by land." Iraqi Shia militias (Kata'ib Sayyid al-Shuhada) have called for a "mass rally" in Baghdad on June 19 to celebrate Iran's victory against "global arrogance."

The Iraqi Oil Ministry announced that its oil fields are prepared to resume extraction operations, gradually increasing output to previous levels. SUMO has contacted customers to nominate tankers for loading Iraqi crude from southern ports. Bassem Al-Badri was appointed as the head of the Iraqi National Security Service.

GULF STATES
Three supertankers, carrying approximately six million barrels of oil, departed Saudi Arabia via the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first such large shipment in weeks following the Iran-US MoU. Iran's President Pezeshkian expressed gratitude to Qatar for its "constructive role" in mediating the agreement. US Vice President JD Vance, however, denied reports that Qatar had released billions of frozen Iranian assets without US approval. The UAE has enacted a new law prohibiting individuals under 15 from using social media platforms. Bahrain's civil defense reported a large fire in Al-Salhiya, while Bahraini authorities were reported to be removing Ashura banners, which are Shiite religious displays.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Iran-US Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) Signed**: Presidents Donald Trump and Masoud Pezeshkian formally signed an MoU ending military operations between the two nations.
2.  **US Lifts Maritime Blockade on Iran**: US CENTCOM announced the immediate lifting of the naval blockade on Iran, with 12.5 million barrels of oil reportedly transiting the Strait of Hormuz in the last 24 hours.
3.  **Iran's 60-Day Free Transit in Hormuz**: Iran's Supreme National Security Council announced a 60-day period during which no fees will be levied for commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, managed by the Persian Gulf Strait Authority.
4.  **IDF Casualty in Southern Lebanon**: Master Sgt. (res.) Alexander Filin, 29, was killed and seven other IDF personnel were wounded by a Hezbollah explosive device in southern Lebanon.
5.  **Israel Establishes "Security Zone" in Lebanon**: The IDF deployed forces up to 10 km deep into southern Lebanon, designating it a "security zone" that Prime Minister Netanyahu insists will be maintained.
6.  **Iran Delays Swiss Talks**: Iran postponed its delegation's travel to Switzerland for follow-up MoU discussions, citing continued Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon.
7.  **Iranian Supreme Leader Approves MoU with Reservations**: Mojtaba Khamenei approved the MoU but stated he initially held a "different view," placing responsibility on President Pezeshkian to safeguard Iranian rights.
8.  **US Vice President Criticizes Israeli Cabinet**: JD Vance publicly admonished Netanyahu's cabinet for attacking Trump and urged Israel to respect the peace process, reminding them of US military aid.
9.  **EU to Consider Lifting Iran Sanctions**: EU Foreign Policy Chief Kaja Kallas indicated the EU would consider lifting nuclear-related sanctions on Iran if a nuclear agreement is reached.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high, particularly in southern Lebanon, where Israel's commitment to maintaining a 10km deep "security zone" directly conflicts with Hezbollah's declared defense of Lebanese territory. The recent IDF casualty and Iran's subsequent delay of Swiss talks underscore the fragility of the broader Iran-US peace efforts. Active flashpoints include southern Lebanon, with continuous cross-border exchanges. The US Vice President's public criticism of Israel, coupled with reports of potential US pressure on weapon shipments, suggests growing friction in the US-Israel relationship, which could impact Israel's operational freedom. Red lines include Israel's unwavering stance on its security zone and Iran's insistence on protecting the "Resistance Front" and its national rights without succumbing to "excessive demands" on its nuclear program or missile capabilities.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**US Posture**: President Trump defended the MoU as an economic success (lower oil prices, rising stocks) and a security victory (Iran won't have nukes). VP JD Vance criticized Israeli cabinet members for attacking Trump, citing significant US military aid to Israel, and called for Israel to "respect this peace process" and avoid "going wild" in Lebanon. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth stated the US military would be the "big stick behind negotiations" and warned of an "iron blockade" if Iran violates nuclear terms. CENTCOM lifted the maritime blockade. The White House submitted the MoU to Congress.
**Gulf States**: Saudi Arabia resumed large oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar was acknowledged by Iran for its mediation role.
**EU Members**: EU Foreign Policy Chief Kaja Kallas indicated the EU would consider lifting nuclear-related sanctions on Iran if a deal is reached, but was criticized by Israeli FM Sa'ar, who severed contact. Bulgarian PM Roman Radev announced a veto on new EU sanctions against Russia.
**Russia**: Russia reported shooting down 555 Ukrainian drones, with flights suspended at Moscow airports due to attacks on the Moscow refinery and a bridge in Crimea. Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov vowed a "decisive and devastating" response to any NATO aggression.
**China**: Warned Israel against obstructing the MoU, urging support for regional peace.
**Turkey**: German intelligence reports accused Turkey (alongside Russia, China, and Iran) of espionage in Berlin. Trump reportedly told Turkish President Erdogan he would attend the July NATO summit only for him.
**Pakistan**: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, a signatory to the MoU, was thanked by Iran for mediation. His planned trip to Switzerland for follow-up talks was canceled, with a deputy expected to attend.
**Tajikistan**: President Emomali Rahmon expressed satisfaction with the end of the war and emphasized stronger bilateral cooperation with Iran.
**France**: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot expressed full support for the diplomatic process and safe shipping in Hormuz. President Emmanuel Macron, however, expressed "many question marks" about the agreement.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
**Contradictions and Unverified Claims**: A significant contradiction exists regarding the "Leader" in Iran; Ghalibaf refers to "Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei" as "martyred leader," while Press TV also mentions the "martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei" in an image caption, despite the Supreme Leader being publicly alive. Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei is identified as the Leader in other contexts, creating confusion about who is being referred to and who is "martyred." Regarding nuclear commitments, US VP Vance claimed Iran committed to "destroying their highly enriched material," which is a stronger assertion than Iran's Foreign Ministry's statement about "reducing enriched materials" as an option, with "transferring enriched materials out of the country" being unacceptable. Trump's characterization of the MoU as "unconditional surrender" by Iran stands in stark contrast to the Iranian narrative of it being a major victory, indicative of propaganda on both sides. VP Vance's wide range ($100-200 billion+) for frozen Iranian assets and his denial of Qatari releases without US approval contradict the Financial Times report of $6 billion being accessible. The differing reasons for the delay of Swiss talks (Iran citing Israeli attacks, Pakistan claiming being told a meeting wasn't needed) suggest a lack of clear communication or coordinated messaging.

**Propaganda Indicators**: Both US (Trump's social media) and Iranian (Pezeshkian, Ghalibaf, Press TV) sources heavily engage in self-praise and victory narratives regarding the MoU, framing it in their favor while dismissing opposing views. VP Vance's public criticism of the Israeli cabinet also serves a dual purpose of asserting US leverage and potentially mitigating Israeli backlash against the MoU's terms.

**Reporting Gaps**: The full, verified text of the MoU is not provided, only excerpts and summaries. Details on the specific fate of all existing sanctions (beyond general commitments and oil export permits) remain unclear. There's a notable disparity in reporting on the scale of conflict in Lebanon; Hezbollah claims "heavy losses" for IDF, while IDF reports are more restrained, confirming one death and seven injuries. Information regarding the broader Syrian conflict, Iraqi internal appointments beyond a few key figures, and the full economic impact on Iraq (beyond oil resumption) is limited.
